# A couple of merged /etc/hosts files -- Klein's and Oxford's.
# Dictionary from Center for Research in Lexicography
# Don Olivier, Harvard School of Public Health
# Don Olivier, Harvard School of Public Health     don@hsph.harvard.edu
# From ftp.nisc.sri.com:/pub/zone  1/93
# From the on-line version of the King James bible, acquired by doing:
# Internet hostnames used more than once, without digit, _, -
# Notably, a.foo-baz.what.edu has been split out as 5 words:
# Some computer companies
# The /etc/hosts file, with some severe hacking done to it.
# This is full of "junk" works
# Words from Programmer's Technical Reference for MSDOS and the IBM PC
# argus.stanford.edu:/netinfo/hosts.txt dated 6/25/92
# cat KJbible/* | tr -cs A-Za-z '\012' | tr A-Z a-z | sort | uniq
# foo, foo-baz, foobaz, what, and edu.  The "a" was not included
# from Bill Kinnersley's Language List 2.2
# from Denis Howe's Free On-line Dictionary of Computing: wombat.doc.ic.ac.uk
# from a technical dictionary (original source unknown)
# from usenet address list pit-manager.mit.edu
# from uunet.uu.net
# ftp.cs.purdue.edu:/pub/pcert/dict/misc/various/
# pockt dictionary world.std.com:/obi/
# since it was only a single letter.
